ORM stands for Object-Relational Mapping. It is a programming technique that acts as a bridge between object-oriented programming languages (like Python or Java) and relational databases (like MySQL or PostgreSQL), allowing developers to create, read, update, and delete data as objects rather than writing SQL queries.

Torch is an older, now largely inactive, machine learning framework that used the Lua programming language, while PyTorch is its modern, widely-adopted successor built for Python. PyTorch leverages the core functionalities of Torch but in a more accessible, Pythonic environment, making it a leading choice for deep learning research and production. 

NLP stands for Natural Language Processing. It is a branch of artificial intelligence (AI) that enables computers to understand, interpret, generate, and manipulate human language (both written text and speech). It bridges the gap between human communication and computer comprehension using techniques like machine learning.

Purpose: To analyze and understand the meaning behind human language to perform tasks.

aiohttp is an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for Python built on asyncio, designed for high-performance AI applications, web scraping, and API services. It facilitates concurrent requests, crucial for handling multiple AI model inferences or fetching data efficiently. 

aiofiles is a Python library used in AI and data-intensive applications to handle local disk file I/O asynchronously, preventing blocking of the asyncio event loop. It enables efficient reading/writing of large datasets or model files without halting concurrent tasks, essential for high-performance I/O-bound applications. 

ASGI stands for Asynchronous Server Gateway Interface. It is a standard interface for Python web servers, frameworks, and applications designed to handle both asynchronous and synchronous code, acting as a modern, high-performance successor to the WSGI (Web Server Gateway Interface) standard.
